title: Benefits & Total Compensation
summary: Learn why job compensation can include more than wages or salary and how benefits, time off, training, retirement contributions, and other employer-provided value may affect a job decision.
objectives: Distinguish wages or salary from total compensation.
Identify common categories of employee benefits.
Compare job offers using more than headline pay alone.

vocab.def: Pay and other value provided in connection with work.
An employer-provided program, service, contribution, or form of support available under applicable terms.
Employer-provided paid leave available under the employer's applicable policy.
The combined value of wages or salary plus applicable employer-provided benefits and other compensation.

sections.heading: Pay is important, but it is not the entire offer
sections.body: Two jobs with similar wages can differ in schedule, paid time off, training, retirement contributions, insurance options, bonuses, or other benefits.

sections.heading: Benefits have rules and eligibility conditions
sections.body: Benefits may depend on employment status, hours, waiting periods, enrollment choices, plan terms, or other conditions.

sections.heading: Compare offers using the full picture
sections.body: Consider pay, schedule, commute, stability, training, advancement, work conditions, benefits, and other factors relevant to your goals.

sections.heading: Read before you assume
sections.body: A benefit name alone does not tell you every cost or condition. Review official plan or employer information before relying on it.

practice.prompt: Job A pays slightly more per hour, while Job B includes paid training and additional benefits. Which job is automatically better?
practice.answer: Neither automatically. Compare the complete compensation package and other job conditions.

practice.prompt: An employer says health coverage is available. Should you assume it costs nothing?
practice.answer: No. Review the actual plan terms, eligibility, costs, and employer contributions.

quiz.question: What does total compensation consider?
options: Pay plus applicable benefits and other employer-provided value
quiz.answer: Pay plus applicable benefits and other employer-provided value

lab.objective: Compare two simulated job offers using wages, schedule, benefits, training, time off, commute, and other relevant factors.

reflectionPrompt: Which job benefit or work condition besides pay would matter most to you, and why?
